rulings.because: Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **1 · journalist** (revise on lines 3–6 vs clear) — **clear.** The two bold lines state two different facts truthfully: "The platform is approved: The Stop Line, decided by Kamen Kamenov" and "The owners and the calendar below are not yet approved; no owner is recorded." The page then opens the door for the second ("Approve the owners and the calendar — Kamen Kamenov before Month 1"). A skeptical reader finds a status, not a contradiction.

Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **2 · upstream-trace** (reject on rows 12–17 citing the toolkit's review cadence vs revise on row 17 citing its rollout) — **revise, not reject.** The map's phase column reads "all phases" for 11 of 13 tactics, including "Earned validation outreach | Hero | all phases", while the toolkit's rollout says the programme "cleans public identity, locks the proof library, tests the owner control message, launches the founder-led proof story and then seeks earned validation" and the page's own phases table places earned validation in Amplify (Months 10, 11, 12). The cell inherits the year-long cadence of the measurement and always-on ownership rows that name every card, so the card's own phase disappears from the map. The rows are real and traceable; the phase cell is what misleads. Revise: show a card's own phase unless the card itself recurs across phases.

Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **3 · journalist** and **4 · employee-insider** (revise on the targets and KPI lines vs clear) — **clear, both.** The targets name who reads what and when ("Month 1: Kamen Kamenov, Matthew Maday and the assigned public-identity owner read the claim register, public-profile conflict list and Key-Message Table before any Month 2 build work starts"), and the KPI names two measures with their scale and instrument ("public-profile conflicts closed — count, public identity cleanup register · AI claims carrying proof owner and stop-line fields — percentage, The Stop Line claim register"). "The assigned public-identity owner" is not a contradiction of the unassigned door: the door says who assigns and by when, and the target says what that person reads once assigned.

Revise: the owners read and react; Kamen approves the launch language in writing.

Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **7 · upstream-trace** (clear vs revise citing the platform's card) — **revise.** The platform page defines the series as "Always-on after launch"; the roadmap narrows it to "Monthly from Month 8 through Month 11" and the proof order splits it into "Month 8 to Month 9 Senior craft story series" and "Month 10 to Month 11 Senior craft story series amplification". Launch is Months 4 and 5, so three post-launch months carry no series and the producer's promise is not preserved. Revise: start the series after launch as the platform states, or record the narrowing as a decision.

Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **8 · journalist**, **9 · employee-insider** and **10 · competitor** (revise on the loop sentence vs clear) — **revise, all three.** The loop runs all year and "deploy[s] the trained advocates", yet the same sentence says the advocates are "equipped by Employee advocacy kit for Conversation Management advocates in Month 11". A year-long loop deploying advocates who receive their kit in the last quarter is a quotable inconsistency; the two upstream-trace seats already agreed it is a defect on this unit, citing the toolkit's "Employee advocacy push". Revise: say when advocates are trained and deployed, or move the kit earlier.

Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **11 · buyer-read** (revise vs clear) — **revise.** The three agreed-defect cells on this unit (journalist, employee-insider, upstream-trace) all revise the same sentence, and the buyer's difficulty is the same: "Month 8 to Month 9 Senior craft story series" appears in the thought-leadership stage and "Month 10 to Month 11 Senior craft story series amplification" in the visibility stage, so one card belongs to two stages and the reader cannot tell which order governs it. Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **12 · cfo** (revise on the two rollout lines vs clear) — **revise.** "Then widen" names the audiences and the assets ("proof pages, technical artifacts, partner packs, earned validation and Signed by Humans advocacy") but not when the widening starts or how long it runs, so a funder cannot place the widening against the calendar; the agreed upstream-trace defect on this unit reads the same gap. Revise: name the month the widening starts (the Launch months 4 and 5) and the phase that carries it.
